question.text: Which of the following statements about position limits across equity, currency, and interest rate derivative segments is correct?

answer.text: SEBI sets the equity derivatives position-limit framework; ETCD limits are governed by SEBI/exchange rules alongside RBI currency directions; ETIRD exchange position-limit guidelines are provided by SEBI, while RBI governs the broader IRD product/participant framework
Position limits are uniformly set by SEBI across all three derivative segments
RBI sets position limits for all three derivative segments as it manages monetary policy
Position limits are set by the exchanges independently without any regulatory prescription

explanation.text: The Logic: Equity derivatives position limits are laid down by SEBI. For exchange-traded currency derivatives (ETCD), limits are governed by SEBI/exchange rules in conjunction with RBI's currency directions. For exchange-traded interest rate derivatives (ETIRD), the workbooks state that exchange position-limit guidelines are provided by SEBI, while RBI governs the wider IRD product and participant framework. The Trap: Treating any single regulator as the sole limit-setter across all three segments misses the cross-segment split, and assuming exchanges set limits independently ignores the SEBI/RBI framework they operate within. Note: The INR 50 billion figure cited in some materials is the collective net-long IRF limit for FPIs, not a bank-specific gross limit.
